title: feat(129): the gate fence; acceptance runs in the world the session worked in, and a refusal is counted where no child can erase it
body:
## Summary

Spec 129 carries the credential fence past the session to every place the engine runs code a repository controls, and moves the refusal count out of the fenced process's reach.

- The gate suite (build preflight and rounds, ship round 3, shepherd round 4), the bracket and the engine's own git in the candidate run with the session's fenced environment (B-1, B-6); in place they get the scrub (B-2). Hooks still run, without a credential.
- Credentialed git (the base fetch, the in-place fast-forward, the broker's ls-remote and push, the verify fetch) runs with `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` (B-7).
- Each shim reports its refusal to the supervisor over a loopback channel whose listener runs on a worker thread and counts before it acknowledges, so the count is final when the command returns and no child can withdraw it (B-3, D-10). The log stays as a legible copy no stage reads.
- A round whose count rose is not accepted and mints no receipt, whatever its commands exited: `acceptance.fence-refused`, reason `gate-fence-refused`, quoted in the remediation prompt (B-4, D-11). `GateEvidence` and the build evidence carry `fence` with an explicit zero; session counts no longer include the gate.
- The verify stage reads acceptance at the base of the run that produced the merge, journals `acceptance.changed` when the head's block differs, runs its lines behind a fence built beside the worktree under the daemon home, and runs browser sessions there too (B-8, B-10, D-13).
- Live acceptance is an operator's journaled allowance: `project.verify.set`, `projects verify <name> fenced|inherit`, `POST /api/projects/<name>/verify`, shown on the project row (B-9, D-14).
- The fence's git config carries the operator's name and email, so fenced commits keep the operator's identity (D-12).

## Testing

- `make gate` exits 0 (coupling OK over 27 paths, coverage 205/205); `make members` exits 0 (typecheck, member builds, 1023 bun tests pass, 0 fail).
- The Verification block, line by line: `gate-fence.test.ts` 15 pass, `build.test.ts` 45, `verify.test.ts` 29, `broker.test.ts` 9, `fence.test.ts` 18, `make gate` 0. The fence suite also passes on Linux (dash as `/bin/sh`) in a Bun container.
- Live round through the production seams (git, make, bun and spec-spine real; GitHub API faked, as for 122 and 125), on a host with a keyring-backed `gh`: a governed fixture gated by `make gate` plus `bun test` built under the fence and minted a receipt; `gh auth token` inside the gate exited 127 and was counted; the broker pushed, opened and merged; the verify stage passed under its fence reading acceptance at the run's base. No gate or acceptance line needed a credential.

title: feat(128): the origin guard; a page in the operator's browser can no longer drive or read the daemon
body:
Stacked on the records PR (`128-132-realignment-rev3`), which carries 128's approval. Merge that one first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

## Summary

Spec 128, the origin guard; `implementation: complete`.

- **The guard.** Before any route runs, the daemon refuses a request that:
  - has a Host that is not a loopback name at the bound port;
  - has an Origin that is present and not the daemon's own;
  - is a preflight;
  - changes state without `X-Api-Version`.

  A refusal answers 403 `forbidden` naming the rule. Refusals are counted on `/api/meta` and never journaled.
- **Credentials in the origin URL.**
  - Both origin lookups drop an https URL's userinfo.
  - Export policy 6 withholds any string containing such a URL, on the TypeScript and Rust sides, which stay byte-identical.
  - Every envelope and streamed payload the API serves is reduced; the journals keep their bytes.
- **Dev UI.** The dev proxy rewrites Origin to the daemon's only for the dev server's own origin, and can target another loopback daemon (`STATECRAFT_DEV_DAEMON_URL`).
- **Regression tests.** The measured attack probes are now tests: foreign, `null` and other-port origins, the rebinding Host, and a token-bearing origin through a receipt, the export, the projects chain, the served views and the SSE replay.
- **Pre-existing defect fixed (D-15, D-16).** The web UI had not rendered in a browser since spec 123, because `api-client.ts` reached `fs`, `path` and `crypto` through `lifecycle-policy.ts`.
  - `policyPayload` moves unchanged into a module with no run-time imports.
  - A new test walks the UI's run-time import graph and fails on any Node or Bun built-in it reaches.

## Testing

- **Gates.**
  - `make gate`: coverage 204/204, couple with no drift.
  - `make members`: typecheck, member builds, 996/996 Bun tests.
  - `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo test -p statecraft-journal`.
- **Verification block.** The spec's commands (origin-guard, server, candidate, projects and export suites; `cargo test -p statecraft-journal`; `make gate`) were run individually, and all passed.
- **Live rounds.** Run in headless Chrome 152 against a throwaway daemon built from this branch (scratch home, unqualified scratch repository):
  - A page on another loopback port posted to `disarm` twice. Both requests were refused, the refusal count went from 0 to 2, and the chain bytes were unchanged.
  - The daemon's own UI journaled `project.disarmed`.
  - Through `bun run web:dev`, the dev UI journaled `project.armed`, and a foreign Origin sent through the proxy was refused.

title: docs(design): 05 checks the realignment against the tree; drafts 128 to 132, and 126 and 127 revised
body:
## What this is

Design record 05 reads the September 11 handoff packet for this repository against the tree at `6f49d9a`, and records what survives as proposals for review. **Nothing here is approved.** D58 to D73 are proposed decisions; 128 to 132 are born `draft`; 126 and 127 stay `draft` with a proposed revision each. No approved spec is edited; every new edge is an additive `extends`.

## Findings the packet did not name (doc 05 section 3)

- **F1, cross-origin control.** The loopback API checks neither `Origin` nor `Host`, the version header is optional, and a `text/plain` body is parsed as JSON. Measured against the API test fixtures: a foreign-origin `text/plain` POST disarmed a project (200, `project.disarmed` journaled), and a foreign `Host` GET was served. Approve, gate, profile and policy routes are reachable the same way. Draft 128.
- **F2, the gate is outside the fence.** `runGate` spawns with no `env`, so candidate-editable gate code runs with the daemon credentials, outside 121 B-3 and 125. Not in 125 section 6. Draft 129; 126 revised.
- **F3, a token in the origin URL leaks.** `originUrl` is verbatim; measured: userinfo passes into `acceptance.receipt` and through the export policy (`withheldFields: []`), is served by the API, and is rendered into every remediation prompt via the capsule. Draft 128.
- **F4, a packaged engine does not work.** Measured with a compiled engine outside the checkout: `/` answers 503 (assets expected at `/web/dist`) and `daemon start` fails (re-spawn passes a source path). 042 D-10 deferred this. Draft 130.
- **F5, no original-bytes receipt exists,** and bundle verification is integrity-only from a self-declared anchor. Draft 132.
- **F6, draft 127 cannot post from a fenced session,** and would publish around the broker if it could. 127 revised.

## Review asks

- Approve or reject each draft separately. 128 and 129 are small, verified and security-relevant; neither depends on another repository.
- 130 D-1 (ship the Rust sensor and drivers, not the TypeScript builds of the same names) is the choice most worth a look.
- The revisions to 126 and 127 are proposals against drafts you already reviewed; each has a dated status note listing exactly what changed.

## Validation

- `make refresh` then `make gate`: check fresh, lint 0 errors 0 warnings, coverage 200/200, codex-kit match; `spec-spine couple --base origin/main --head HEAD` OK, 8 paths, no drift.
- The 20 index warnings are units the drafts will create (19 files or directories, and the pending Makefile section of 127).
- Suites the packet cited rerun: fence, receipt and broker 26 pass, 133 assertions; candidate, export, handoff, API server and static 95 pass, 667 assertions. Fixture scope only.
- An independent read-only fact-check of about 95 claims found three citation errors, all corrected before commit.
- Probes ran in a scratch directory against test fixtures and a compiled engine on spare ports; nothing touched a real remote or the running daemon, and no probe is committed.

title: docs(127): the review note, so a pull request shows what the local cycle found
body:
Files spec **127-pr-review-note** as a `draft` (`implementation: pending`).
Nothing is built here. Approval is a human flip.

## The gap

This repository reviews locally. `/code-review` runs in the session against the
diff, the gate runs in the exact chain CI runs, and a finding is either fixed or
consciously accepted. **None of that reaches the pull request.** A reviewer
opening one sees three green checks, a title and a body, and cannot tell a
change that was reviewed and had two findings fixed from one pushed without a
glance. The PRs for 109 and 126 both looked exactly like that, which is where
this came from.

## Why not a CI comment

The obvious fix is the wrong one. A CI job that comments the gate results
restates what the checks UI already renders better, and it **cannot see the
local review at all**, because the review happened on a machine CI never
touches. What is missing is not a second rendering of `pass`; it is the
session's own knowledge.

So the session posts it: one comment per pull request, found by an HTML marker
and updated in place on every push.

## What the note carries

| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| head | the sha the note describes, and when it was written |
| changed | one line, in the same voice as the commit |
| gate | each command that actually ran, with its exit code |
| review | every finding as `file:line`, severity, and disposition (`fixed` with the fixing sha / `accepted` with the reason / `deferred` with where it went) |

## Three load-bearing properties

**Absence is stated, never implied (B-3).** `no findings` and `not run` never
collapse into one another, and a gate half that did not apply reads `not
applicable`, not a blank. This is 125 D-3 and kit 082's `not read` versus `none`
applied here: a missing line must not read as an absence of findings to someone
deciding whether to look closer.

**The note never invents a verdict (B-4).** The script reports the exit codes
and findings it is handed. It does not run the gate and does not infer a result
from a green check. Given nothing, it says nothing ran.

**Posting is not a gate (B-5).** A failure to post is reported and never fails
the ship. A ship stage that dies on a comment teaches the next session to skip
the step, which provides no visibility at all.

## D-5: the orphan secret becomes a decision

This repository carries a `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` secret, added 2026-07-23,
that **nothing uses**. Measured 2026-09-10:

```
gh secret list                     CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN  2026-07-23
grep -rn CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN   (repo)                   none
grep -rn anthropics/claude         .github/                 none
grep -rln 'AI review'              specs/ docs/ standards/  none
.github/workflows/                 ci, members, release, spec-spine
```

That was a gap, not a decision. D-5 makes it a decision and gives its reason:
the local cycle reviews **before** the push, inside the loop that can act on a
finding, at no CI minutes and no round trip; a CI review would arrive after the
push and lengthen every iteration. The token is left unused deliberately.
Removing the secret is a separate operator action this spec does not require,
and a later session that wants a CI review amends D-5 rather than discovering an
unexplained secret and guessing.

## Placement

The instruction lands in `AGENTS.md` "Working the backlog", not in a skill:
109 §3.1 requires every `SKILL.md` byte-identical to the kit, and `AGENTS.md` is
where this repo's project layer belongs (110 and 118 already extend it). It is
also read by every agent, not only Claude, which matters for a step D-2 admits
can be skipped.

## Gate

`spec-spine compile` 0 warnings across 71 specs, `lint --fail-on-warn` exit 0,
`make gate` exit 0. Three files: the spec and its two shards.

title: docs(126): the sandboxed executor, authored draft from doc 04 §11 and 125 §6
body:
Files spec **126-sandboxed-executor** as a `draft` (`implementation: pending`).
Nothing is built here. Approval is a human flip.

**Revised on owner review before approval.** Three points were raised and each
is now settled with a measurement rather than an argument. The original
rationale for D-3 and B-3 did not survive; what replaced them is below.

## Why a shim could not have done it

The three residuals of 125 §6 share a shape the fence could not reach, because
a shim is a file on `PATH` and every residual goes around `PATH`:

| Residual | Why `PATH` is irrelevant |
|---|---|
| `HOME` readable (`~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`, the keyring) | a config file is read, not executed |
| absolute path bypasses `PATH` | `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh` never consults it |
| `~/.ssh` keys on disk | a directory, not a command |

Neither provider can be asked to do it either: the Claude driver's permission
modes gate prompts and do not fence the filesystem (120 D-2), and Codex's
`--sandbox workspace-write` confines **writes** while every residual here is a
read or an exec. So the engine applies its own confinement at the spawn in
`driver.ts` where 125 already overlays the fence.

## The three revisions

**1. D-3: signing is brokered; the spec asserts nothing about unsigned commits.**
The earlier draft had the candidate commit unsigned, reasoning that every commit
on `main` is committed and signed by GitHub because the squash merge is created
server-side. That is true and insufficient: it describes a *merged* commit, not
whether a head branch carrying unsigned commits is accepted. Measured: this
repository has `required_signatures` **enabled** on `main`, with `enforce_admins`
enabled. Rather than settle it by experiment on a protected branch, B-5 removes
the dependency on the answer. Signing becomes a brokered act, the shape 122 gave
publication: the candidate's `gpg.ssh.program` is a helper holding no key that
forwards to the daemon, the daemon signs **outside** the sandbox and journals
`broker.sign`. Commits stay signed, provenance is preserved, the key never
enters the confined process, and an unreachable signer fails the stage rather
than quietly producing unsigned commits. Handing the key to the session was
rejected, and was never the only alternative.

**2. D-6: the keychain deny would have broken Claude. Removed.**
Measured on the authoring machine:

```
~/.claude/.credentials.json                 absent
keychain item "Claude Code-credentials"     exists
  lookup on host                            exit 0   (reachable)
  lookup under a SecurityServer deny        exit 44  (broken)
~/.codex/auth.json                          present  (Codex unaffected)
```

Claude Code keeps **no** credentials file on macOS and authenticates from that
keychain, so the earlier B-3 would have broken provider authentication on every
driven session. The service deny is gone; the `/usr/bin/security` CLI deny
stays. §6 now carries the keyring-through-the-Security-framework as a residual
this spec closes **only ergonomically**, rather than claiming it closed. That
residual is the strongest argument for the brokered file service that follows.

**3. B-6/D-7: containment is an operator policy, not a best effort.**
`required` refuses a run whose containment is unavailable, so unattended
operation can rely on "Statecraft is running" implying "containment is in
force". `preferred` degrades and journals. `sandboxMode` records which was in
force, so an uncontained run is legible rather than indistinguishable from a
contained one.

## Acceptance was rewritten with them

Shell probes establish that a mechanism *can* deny a path. They do not establish
that a provider still works, and §5 no longer accepts on them. It now requires
live **Claude and Codex** sessions that authenticate, build, and publish through
the broker under the sandbox; the four reaches confirmed closed from inside a
real session; and the policy exercised both ways.

## What it does not claim

Publication stays autonomous: confining the session removes no capability from
the engine (B-7), so no human pushes or merges by hand. Still open and stated in
§6: the brokered file service, the keyring through the framework, network
access, a secret already in context, Linux as a *qualified* platform, and
anything the operator launches outside this engine. Known compatibility effect,
recorded rather than discovered later: SSH-authenticated dependency fetching
inside a session breaks.

## Gate

`spec-spine compile` 0 warnings across 70 specs, `lint --fail-on-warn` exit 0,
`make gate` exit 0.

title: chore(109): adopt kit 082; a refusal no longer spends a remediation round
body:
Adopts spec-spine kit spec 082, "a refusal is not a remediation round", the
separate decision spec 109 §6 said it would take. Recorded as 109 D-1.

## What changes in the loop

`/shepherd` now classifies a red required check before it edits anything, and
a CRITICAL finding is reported to a human having consumed **no** remediation
round. Exactly four things are CRITICAL:

1. a coupling refusal whose only remedy is editing a foreign spec, or a
   `Spec-Drift-Waiver:`;
2. a hand-edited derived artefact (as opposed to the regeneration the gate
   itself prescribes);
3. a dependency cycle;
4. an ambient input (clock, environment, unordered map, filesystem order)
   reaching a hashed path.

The two-round bound (spec-spine 048 §3.1) is unchanged. What changed is that
a refusal no longer spends one of the two. The handoff report gains a
`Classification:` line, and its thread line reads `not read` when the run
stopped at CRITICAL, rather than `none`, which would claim an absence the run
never checked.

## Provenance

`.claude/skills/shepherd/SKILL.md` is copied verbatim from
`<spec-spine>/kit/.claude/skills/shepherd/SKILL.md` at spec-spine `9438a06`.
That is the only kit file 082 changed, and the newest commit touching `kit/`:
spec-spine 083 (`17c368e`) files a draft against `spec-spine attest` and ships
no kit change, so this leaves the kit fully caught up rather than one skill
behind again. 109 §3.1's byte-identity requirement holds: `diff -r` is empty
across all ten skills.

## The crossing, and why it needs no waiver

The Codex face is generated from the Claude one, so `scripts/codex-kit.py`
rewrites `.agents/skills/shepherd/SKILL.md` (owned by 118) and
`.codex/kit-manifest.json` (owned by 123); `make gate`'s kit check refuses
until it has. That is declared as two `extends` edges on 109 rather than by
editing 118 or 123, which is the door `adversarial-prompt-refusal.md` names
for touching a unit another spec owns. It amends neither spec and needs no
waiver.

The skills edge is claimed at directory granularity (`.agents/skills/`, the
same shape 118 uses to establish it) rather than at the single file 082
changed: every kit update regenerates whichever skills moved, so a per-file
edge would need widening by hand each time.

Both mirror files are hashed governance inputs, which is why every shard's
`shardHash` rotates in this diff. No shard was hand-edited.

## Gate

`make gate` exits 0 (`couple`: 4 paths checked, no drift), `make kit-check`
exits 0 including `codex-kit.test.py`. No verb, flag or pinned version moves:
082 is skill prose, `[meta] required_version` stays 0.18.0. It does not touch
the agents that carry this repo's project layer, so this kit update needed no
merge step (109 §3.6).

The cargo and bun halves do not apply: nothing under `src/`, `tests/` or
`members/` is touched.

title: feat(125): the credential fence; the broker becomes the only path that works
body:
Builds spec 125, approved by the owner on 2026-09-10. Closes doc 04 §11's
first open limit and the one 122 recorded three times (B-7, §5, D-4).

## The problem was wider than 122 named

| Reach | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` in the environment | closed (122 B-7) | closed |
| `gh` resolving from the system keyring | **open** | closed |
| `git push` over SSH via `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` or `~/.ssh` | **open, and unnamed** | closed |

`origin` on this repository is an ssh URL, so the second reach was live and
no deny list could ever have closed it: neither is environment-variable
shaped.

## What landed

- **`fence.ts`** builds a directory beside the candidate (never inside it, or
  121 B-4's clean-tree rule would fail every receipt) holding refusing `gh`
  and `ssh` shims and a gitconfig with no credential helper and
  `core.sshCommand` pointed at the fenced `ssh`.
- **The overlay** puts that `bin` first on `PATH` and redirects
  `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`,
  `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` and both askpass hooks. `HOME` is deliberately
  untouched; both providers authenticate from it and 014 B-2 depends on that.
- **`CHILD_ENV_DENY` goes four to six**, adding the ssh agent, one list on
  both sides of the wire as 121 B-3 has it.
- **The fence rides on the session request** (D-2), because the daemon builds
  the driver before a candidate exists. Build, ship and shepherd all get it
  through the runner they already share.
- **A refusal is journaled.** The three stages fold the count into their
  evidence and emit `fence.refused`, which joins the export allowlist at
  policy version 5 **on both the TypeScript and Rust sides**. The parity test
  caught the two copies disagreeing before this landed, which is 039 FR-003
  doing its job.

## The property is integrity, not confidentiality

An agent told to ship runs `gh pr create` because it is the obvious move, and
122's prompt asking it not to is a request rather than a boundary. Every such
publish is unreceipted, unleased and invisible to the journal. The fence
makes the obvious move fail and name the broker, so the only path that works
is the one that is recorded.

§6 keeps three residuals honest rather than hiding them: `HOME` stays
readable, an absolute path bypasses `PATH`, and `~/.ssh` keys stay on disk.
Closing those is doc 04 §11's sandboxed executor, not this spec.

## Evidence

13 fence cases prove it from **inside** a real candidate rather than
asserting over the object the engine built, in 124's negative-suite idiom,
including that a push to a local bare remote still succeeds (the fence closes
credentials, not git) and that a tampered shim is overwritten on reopen.

The live round, on this host (`gh auth status`: keyring; `origin`: ssh):

```
outside fence: gh auth token -> exit 0, token obtained
inside  fence: gh auth token -> exit 127, nothing, broker message, tallied
inside  fence: gh api user   -> exit 127, empty body
broker push -> remote head == candidate head (real bare remote, production git seam)
broker.action push   intent / outcome ok=true
broker.action openPr intent / outcome ok=true
```

## Gate

`make gate` 0, `make members` 0 (976 pass, 0 fail), `cargo fmt --check` 0,
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` 0, `cargo test` 0. Six decisions
recorded in §7.

title: docs(125): the credential fence, authored draft from doc 04 §11
body:
Authors spec 125 from doc 04 §11's open limits. **No code**: this is the
spec only, born `draft` / `pending`, so approval stays a human flip
(`AGENTS.md` step 1).

## What it closes

122 established the action boundary and recorded a known limit in three
places (B-7, §5, D-4): a `gh` authenticated through a keyring still answers
in the candidate. Reading this machine shows the limit is **wider than 122
named**:

| Reach | Denied today? |
|---|---|
| `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` in the environment | yes, since 122 B-7 |
| `gh` resolving its token from the system keyring | **no** (`gh auth status`: keyring, scopes `repo`, `workflow`) |
| `git push` over SSH via `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` or `~/.ssh` | **no** (`origin` is `git@github.com:...`) |

Neither of the last two is environment-variable shaped, and `CHILD_ENV_DENY`
can only remove what it names.

## The approach

Construct the child's credential environment instead of filtering it: a
fence directory first on `PATH` whose `gh` and `ssh` refuse and name the
broker, `git` redirected to a candidate-owned config with no credential
helper and no agent, and `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` / `SSH_AGENT_PID` joining the deny
list (four names to six, one list on both sides as 121 B-3 has it). The
fence lives beside the candidate, never inside it, so it cannot dirty the
tree 121 B-4 requires clean before a receipt.

## What the property actually is

**Integrity, not confidentiality.** The threat model is a *capable* session,
not a hostile one: an agent told to ship runs `gh pr create` because it is
the obvious move, and 122's prompt asking it not to is a request rather than
a boundary. Every such publish is unreceipted, unleased and invisible to the
journal. The fence makes the obvious move fail with a message naming the
broker, so the only path that works is the one that is recorded.

## What it does not close, recorded rather than hidden

§6 names three residuals honestly: `HOME` stays readable (both providers
authenticate from it, and 014 B-2 depends on that), an absolute path
bypasses `PATH`, and `~/.ssh` keys stay on disk. Each wants doc 04 §11's
sandboxed executor with a brokered file service, which is a larger sequence
and explicitly not this spec.

## Gate

`make gate` exits 0. The two `W-001` unresolved units are the files 125
claims but has not built yet, which is exactly the case
`--fail-on-unresolved` is deliberately off for (109 §3.2, spec 108's
precedent). `registry plan` now reports `1 ready`.

title: chore(109): ratify (draft -> approved)
body:
109-governed-harness was the corpus's only `draft`, carrying
`implementation: complete` with every unit it establishes already on disk
(`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `Makefile`, `.mcp.json`, `.claude/skills|agents|rules`).
Its own Status note said approval is a human flip. The owner made it on
2026-09-10.

Doc 04 §8 (D56, D57). The last of the six.

body:
## 122: the action boundary

Doc 04 §6 (D50 to D52).

### What changes

- **The broker (B-2 to B-5).** `broker.ts`: `push`, `openPr` and `merge`, each admitted by the lease (the run is the project's live run in the folded state) and by the newest receipt covering the head, `openPr` also by 017's marker rules. Every effect journals `broker.action` intent and outcome naming the action, target, head and receipt hash; a refusal journals `broker.refused`. Reconciliation first: a remote already at the head, an open PR at the head, or a merged PR answer `already` with no effect; a diverged remote or a moved PR head is refused.
- **The session proposes (B-1, B-6).** The ship prompt (version 3) tells the session to gate, review, commit and write the PR title and body into the drop box; the engine reads the proposal, receipts the head the session left when the build's receipt no longer covers it (D-5, the same gate over the stable candidate), pushes and opens through the broker, and keeps 017's outside verification. The idempotent precheck is the broker answering `already`. Shepherd merges through the broker on the receipt covering the PR head; after a remediation the session commits and stops, and the engine gates, receipts and pushes the fix.
- **No publish credential in the candidate (B-7).** `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` join the deny list on both sides of the wire (fixture: four names). A keyring-backed `gh` remains reachable; recorded as the known limit.
- **Compatibility.** Without a broker the stages keep the pre-122 flow (D-7); the production deps always build one over the work journal.

title: feat(120): the capability contract, a closed token vocabulary; required refuses before spawn, preferred degrades in the journal
body:
## 120: the capability contract

The design doc 03 D39 deferred, decided in doc 04 §4 (D44 to D46).

### What changes

- **The vocabulary (B-1).** `Capability` in the contract crate: `tool-allowlist`, `max-turns`, `mcp-config`, `cost`, `workspace-write`, `hook-enforcement`, mirrored in `capabilities.ts` and asserted against the `capabilities.json` fixture on both sides.
- **Manifests declare support (B-2).** `capabilities` on the manifest; the tier is derived from the four request tokens and a manifest whose tier disagrees is refused by both parsers. Claude declares the four plus `hook-enforcement` (not `workspace-write`: `acceptEdits` does not fence the filesystem, D-2). Codex declares `workspace-write` and `hook-enforcement`. A manifest without the field is an older member and is read by its tier.
- **Requests state needs (B-3, B-4).** `requirements: {required, preferred}` on the wire; the profile gains `require`, set with `--require <tokens>` on `projects add` and `projects profile`, shown in the detail and the posture cell.
- **Required refuses, preferred degrades (B-5).** The seam reads the manifest before spawning. A required token the driver lacks journals `driver.refused` and returns a synthesized `crashed` with no process started; a preferred one journals `driver.degraded` and the session runs. 043 B-6's mcp-config refusal is now an instance of this rule.
- **Effective configuration is evidence (B-6).** `session.init` carries `applied` beside `degraded`, derived once (`SpawnSpec::requested`) so both drivers and the in-process session agree.

### Evidence

- members: 912 pass; workspace green; clippy and fmt clean; `make gate` green; `spec-spine verify 120` passed.
- Live, through the production deps: a guarded project `--driver codex --require tool-allowlist` was refused before spawn with `driver.refused`; with `--require workspace-write` the real Codex 0.153.4 completed one fast-tier turn, `session.init` reading `applied: ["workspace-write","hook-enforcement"]`, `degraded: ["tool-allowlist","cost"]`.

### Notes

A guarded Codex posture now reports `tool-allowlist` degraded even without an explicit list (the baseline is a list it cannot apply); 117's test says so. Every driver's first session is preceded by one manifest read.

## 119: the floor, the head, the denial

Opens the governed-substrate sequence (doc 04): this PR lands the design record and specs 119 to 124, born approved on the corpus owner's instruction of 2026-09-09, and builds 119.

### What changes

- **The gate floor is read-only (D42).** `gateFloor(base)` is `spec-spine check --fail-on-warn`, `lint --fail-on-warn`, `couple --base <sha> --head HEAD`. The base is resolved to a commit once per stage (`origin/<branch>` after a fetch, the local branch when no remote answers) and journaled in `stage.build.bracket`, `stage.build.gate` and `stage.shepherd.base`. The Claude provider reads a flagged `tool_result` matching the hook-blocked rule; the Codex provider reads a refused `command_execution` item and, per D-6, the tool router's stderr line, which is the only structured signal Codex emits for a blocked command. ## Summary

The last spec of doc 03's plan (D40): the governed kit's Codex face, generated from the Claude one so the two cannot drift, with its gate proven in a driven session rather than assumed.

- **Generated, not imported (B-1 to B-3, B-5, D-2)**: `scripts/codex-kit.py` writes `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (ten byte-identical copies), `.codex/agents/<name>.toml` (name, description and the unchanged body as `developer_instructions`) and `.codex/hooks.json` (the four hooks of `.claude/settings.json`, same matchers, each command wrapped once: stdin read into a variable, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` exported from its `cwd`, the original command run unchanged as a function fed that JSON, so a blocking `exit 2` still blocks). `--check` names any drift and is the spec's verification; `make codex-kit` regenerates. The desktop's stale import (five old skills, `.Codex/rules/` artifacts) is replaced.
- **Two captured facts decided the design**: Codex's hook wire is Claude's (`hook_event_name`, `tool_name: "Bash"`, `tool_input.command`, `cwd`, no project-dir variable), so the PR gate ports unchanged. And a project's hooks run only when trusted, else are skipped with nothing on the stream. So the Codex driver's argv gains `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` (B-4, D-3): for a session the orchestrator drives over a governed checkout, the hooks are the guard, and the flag makes them run.
- **Hashed and documented (B-6, B-7)**: `.codex/**`, `.agents/**` and `scripts/**` join the index's hashed inputs; AGENTS.md's Available Commands names the Codex face, the generator, and why the hooks run.
- **FR-003 by hand**: a clone on a branch that edits `src/main.rs` without its spec; the generated PR gate, fed the captured PreToolUse JSON with `gh pr create` and no project-dir variable, exited 2 with `[pr-gate] BLOCKED: a committed shard tree is stale`.
- **The driven session (AC, D40)**: `statecraft-driver-codex session run` over that fixture, asked to run `gh pr create --title t --body b`. The stream carried the refusal as the agent's own message (`Command blocked by PreToolUse hook: [pr-gate] BLOCKED ...`), the stderr tail carried Codex's router error, and `gh` never ran. The control run without the flag ran `gh pr create` unrefused. Recorded for 116's table: a hook refusal ends the turn as `turn.completed`, so it classifies `completed` and is read from the stream and `resultTextTail`, the same rule order the Claude driver has.

## Summary

The one engine change a second driver needs (doc 02 §11, doc 03 D38): the driver is part of the posture. Nothing else in the engine learns the word `codex`.

- **The field (B-1)**: `ExecutionProfile.driver?: "claude" | "codex"`; the payload emits it as the name or `null` (032 B-5's explicit-null rule), the parser accepts absence, and refuses any other value naming the accepted drivers. The legacy and default-registration profiles carry none, so absence stays the default rather than a materialized `claude`.
- **Set and shown (B-2)**: `--driver <name>` on `projects add` and `projects profile`, refused without a posture the way a model pair is; the detail view gains a `driver:` line after `models:`; the posture cell appends ` via codex` only when set, so a default project's list row is byte-identical to before (the pinned CLI test proves it). The API's `POST .../profile` message names the field; the payload already carried the whole profile.
- **Late-bound (B-3, D-2)**: `createProfileDriver({profile, env})` in `driver.ts` resolves the `ProfileSource` at every call, picks `profile.driver ?? DEFAULT_DRIVER_NAME`, and keeps one process driver per name. `createProductionDaemonDeps` uses it, so the build/ship/shepherd runner, the browser verifier and the daemon's `runSession` follow the profile per spawn, the promise 032 B-4 made for the mode. The scheduler caches deps per project for the process's life, which is why an eager read was rejected. The synthesis session in the CLI passes the name from the folded project.
- **Both sides journal it (B-5)**: the Rust `Profile` gains `driver`, emits and reads it; the 111 wire fixture is regenerated with `"driver": "codex"` and both parsers read it; 114's and 116's parity tests are unchanged and green.
- **Tests**: profile (payload, parse, refusal, render, legacy), driver façade (name per call, one driver per name, kill reaches all), CLI (both verbs, refusal, detail line, unchanged list row), Rust round-trip, and the owned `project-driver.test.ts`: the production deps with the Rust Codex driver and a fake Claude member in a managed directory, the first session to Codex and the second to Claude after the profile source flipped, no rebuild between.

title: feat(specs): author 008 member-dispatch, the umbrella's local face
body:
## Summary

Every verb this binary has is a client of a hosted control plane through
`api.rs` and `auth.rs`. There is no local-execution verb and no notion of a
member. That gap is the whole of the transition described in
claude-observatory's `docs/design/01-umbrella-cli-and-member-seams.md`: the
orchestrator, its `~/.claude` sensor and its Claude driver become member
binaries this CLI dispatches to.

Spec 008 gives the umbrella its second face:

- **Discovery.** An unknown top-level token resolves to `statecraft-<name>`,
  searched in a managed member directory first and `PATH` second. The managed
  directory wins so a member installed through the umbrella is not silently
  shadowed by an unrelated binary earlier on `PATH`; `members list` names the
  location each was found in, so the choice stays auditable.
- **Manifest before trust.** Every candidate's `--member-manifest` is read
  during discovery, before anything is dispatched to. A candidate that does
  not parse is listed as refused with the reason and is never executed again.
- **Dispatch keyed on the member's name**, not on one of its verbs. Doc 01 D15
  reads `statecraft-<verb>` in the git-plugin idiom; taken literally that puts
  every member's verbs in one flat namespace competing with each other and
  with the built-ins. Keying on the name keeps git's discovery mechanism and
  makes collisions structurally impossible.
- **Exit codes verbatim.** A dispatched member's code is returned unchanged,
  which is what makes the umbrella optional rather than lock-in. Dispatch-layer
  failures take a reserved range no member emits: 64 not found, 65 manifest
  refused, 66 contract skew, 67 subverb not declared.
- **Account-less.** No dispatch path reads a credential, calls `auth.rs`, or
  needs a base URL, and a test asserts dispatch succeeds with both absent. The
  local half is the free half; making it depend on the paid half would invert
  the model the split exists to serve.
- **No shell, ever**, and no buffering of member output, because the engine's
  watch verbs stream and a buffered watch is a broken watch.

## Cross-repo

The member side is claude-observatory spec 042 (that repo's PR #72), authored
in the same session. Unlike specs 003 and 004, where the control plane's spec
wins because the plane is the authority, these two are halves of one decision:
neither is the authority, and a divergence between them is a defect in both.
The manifest's `contract` field is what makes a mismatch detectable at runtime.

## Authored as draft

The pair resolves a collision between two shipped contracts: claude-observatory
023 D-4 reads exit `2` as an unreachable daemon, while this repo's spec 002
taxonomy and clap both read `2` as usage. Remapping at the boundary was
rejected (it would make `statecraft engine status` and `statecraft-engine
status` disagree); changing either shipped taxonomy was rejected (both are
tested). The resolution is to pass through, declare each member's taxonomy in
its manifest, and move umbrella failures to 64+. That class of call belongs to
a human, so both specs are `status: draft` and should be ratified together or
neither.

## Testing

- `spec-spine compile`: 9 specs, 0 warnings.
- `spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 info.
- `spec-spine index check`: fresh, with 1 `W-001` for the

title: fix(006): resolve chassis pins per package, not in lockstep
body:
## Summary

The chassis packages moved from the retired `@enrahitu` scope to `@statecrafting` and are now versioned independently: `@statecrafting/toolchain` is published at 0.1.0/0.2.0/0.3.0 while `@statecrafting/hiqlite-native` and `@statecrafting/kernel-native` remain at 0.1.0. Spec 006's original model resolved one target and pinned it to every chassis package, which would have pinned the companions to a version they never published (and failed the lockfile refresh).

This replaces that with per-package resolution:

- A seed (a package the contract names in `[requires]`) resolves the greatest published version its named range allows.
- A companion (in the chassis scope but unnamed) resolves within a caret of its current pin, so it never crosses its own major silently and is never pinned to a nonexistent version.
- `--to` overrides the primary seed only; every other package auto-resolves. The compat gate applies to the forced primary target.
- The runner accepts both `npm view --json` shapes (array, and the bare single-version string some npm builds return).

Per the coherence guard, spec 006 was amended first (per-package model in §2; as-built record and live check in §5), then the code. `implementation` flips to `complete`.

title: feat(006): template upgrade verb (chassis upgrades as a governed local verb)
body:
## Summary

Implements spec 006: `stagecraft template upgrade`, the chassis upgrade as a governed verb. Run in a stamped app checkout, it reads `template.toml`, bumps the chassis package pins in `package.json`, refreshes the lockfile, runs the reserved codemod hook, runs the verify verb of the contract, and commits on a `template-upgrade/<from>-<to>` branch. The enrahitu spec 018 gate (chassis packages published at v0.1.0) is cleared, so this verb is no longer parked.

- **The one local governed verb.** Unlike the spec 004 verbs, `template upgrade` never calls the control plane. It orchestrates a repo-local operation; all structure knowledge stays in the template and its packages. This is the boundary that keeps the CLI from becoming a build daemon (spec 006 summary). It still renders the shared `{ok,data|error}` envelope, so both faces stay uniform and a later fleet-wide sweep can consume the result.
- **Compat gate is the range named by the contract.** A target outside the `[requires]` chassis range is the "major upgrade requires the migration path" refusal (`incompatible_target`); the version policy lives in the template, not the CLI. When a contract names more than one range, the target must satisfy all of them.
- **Chassis discovery is scope-derived, not hardcoded.** Seeds are the `package.json` deps that a `[requires]` key names by unscoped tail (so `node` drops out and `toolchain` resolves to `@enrahitu/toolchain`); the bump set is every exact-pinned dep sharing the scope of a seed, catching companions like `@enrahitu/hiqlite-native` with no `@enrahitu` literal in the CLI.
- **Refusals are structured** (all exit 1, JSON `error.kind`): `not_stamped`, `pre_chassis`, `local_chassis` (chassis present but `file:`-linked, i.e. a template-dev tree), `bad_target`, `incompatible_target`, `dirty_tree`. A verify failure is a completed run whose `{ok:true,data}` result carries `verify:"fail"` and exits 1 (matching `stamp status --watch`), leaving the branch uncommitted for inspection.
- **Offline by construction.** Every git/npm/node side effect sits behind a `Runner` trait, so `cargo test` never gates on the outside world (the spec 003 section 1 discipline).

**Spec 006 stays `implementation: in-progress`** (same shape as 003/004/005): the section 3 live check needs a real stamped app carrying published-version chassis pins plus a newer template release to upgrade across, and the enrahitu scaffold verb (spec 014) is still v0 and edits no dependencies, so no such app exists yet. A dated section 5 Status note records the v1 decisions and exactly what remains (the live upgrade transcript, no code change).

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test`: 117 pass (101 unit + 16 integration). New coverage (all offline, every git/npm/node effect behind a `Runner` fake): scope-derived discovery with companions, the `pre_chassis`/`local_chassis`/`not_stamped`/`incompatible_target`/`dirty_tree` refusals, the multi-range gate, format-preserving pin rewrite, the dry-run plan that mutates nothing, latest-resolution when `--to` is omitted, the no-op that still bumps a companion left behind the primary, the happy path (branch to lock to verify to commit), the verify-failure path that leaves the branch uncommitted, and the result envelope staying `{ok:true,data:{verify:"fail"}}` with a Rendered exit 1. Three end-to-end binary checks drive the offline paths (not-stamped, pre-018, dry-run) with the process working directory set to a fixture.
- An independent review pass ran on the diff before commit and drove hardening. It caught the verify-fail JSON envelope emitting a novel `{ok:false,data}` third shape; fixed to keep the two-shape contract of the codebase as `{ok:true,data:{verify:"fail"}}` plus a Rendered exit 1, matching how `stamp status --watch` renders a terminal `failed` job. Also fixed, each locked with a test: the no-op check now compares every chassis pin (a companion left behind the primary is still bumped), the dirty-tree preflight now runs before target resolution (fail fast, no wasted registry read), and the compat gate checks every named `[requires]` range. Two review notes were accepted and documented in spec section 5 rather than coded (the scope-sweep lockstep assumption; Cargo-flavored semver reading bare ranges as caret, so contract ranges must carry an explicit operator).
- `spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn` (0/0/0), `index check` (fresh): green. `couple` reports the expected spec-002 drift (below).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: this PR implements spec 006 (the template upgrade verb) but necessarily edits files under the spec 002 crate scaffold: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, src/cli.rs, src/commands.rs, src/verbs/template.rs. The `[package.metadata.spec-spine]` key of the crate couples the whole crate to spec 002, so every feature spec code lands in 002 territory (including its own new module file); the new logic lives in the spec-006-owned stagecraft_cli::verbs::template module, and the scaffold edits are the command-tree wiring (a new `template upgrade` subcommand and its dispatch) that spec 002 placed the tree specifically to receive. No 002 design is contradicted, so this is a coupling waiver, not a coherence override.

title: feat(005): MCP stdio server exposing the governance verbs as tools
body:
## Summary

Implements spec 005: `stagecraft mcp` runs a Model Context Protocol server over
stdio, exposing the spec 004 governance verbs as nine MCP tools so a coding
agent (Claude Code first) operates under Stagecraft governance natively, with
the same auth, the same guards, and the same JSON shapes as the CLI face.

- **Not a privileged side door.** Each tool calls the identical spec 004 verb
  request. The endpoint and body knowledge now lives once, in `*_request`
  functions in `stagecraft_cli::verbs` that both faces share; the MCP face only
  chooses which to call. The tool result is the spec 004 §5.2 `{ok,data|error}`
  envelope verbatim, so platform attestation/record ids in the payload are
  carried through for agent transcripts to cite.
- **Guards pass through unchanged.** `stamp_new` requires an explicit `posture`
  and `fleet_remove` a `confirm_name`; both are rejected as JSON-RPC
  invalid-params (-32602) when missing, empty, or malformed. Neither `login` nor
  `install-url --open` is exposed, so an agent can never trigger a browser flow.
- **Unauthenticated is graceful.** The server still starts with no credential
  (or an unreadable one) and answers every tool call with a structured
  `{ok:false,error:{kind:"unauthenticated"}}` result naming `stagecraft login`.
- **Robust transport.** One malformed stdio line (invalid UTF-8, invalid JSON,
  a non-request object) is answered with the right JSON-RPC error and skipped,
  never aborting the server; one current-thread runtime is reused across the
  sequential request loop.
- `stagecraft mcp --print-config` prints the `.mcp.json` install snippet.

**Transport decision (spec 005 §1 amendment):** hand-rolled JSON-RPC 2.0 over
newline-delimited stdio, not the rmcp SDK. The framing is small,
dependency-free, keeps the tree rustls-only, and lets the envelope be the
literal tool result with no reshaping. Recorded in the spec.

**Spec 005 stays `implementation: in-progress`** (same shape as 003 and 004):
the §2 live check needs a running control plane (Stagecraft's tenants/factory/
fleet services are all still `implementation: pending`) plus a Claude Code
`claude mcp add` round-trip. A dated §4 Status note records exactly what
remains; all mock-testable acceptance holds and drops the live transcript in
with no code change once a plane exists.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test`: 98 pass (85 unit + 13 integration). New coverage: a scripted
  in-process stdio client drives `initialize -> tools/list -> tools/call`
  round-trips against a mock-backed verb layer (tenants list, stamp launch with
  posture forwarding, fleet remove with confirm-name forwarding), guard
  rejections for the two guarded tools, the unauthenticated tool-result,
  record-id passthrough, and the transport-robustness paths (invalid UTF-8 line
  survived + next request served, invalid-request vs parse-error codes, explicit
  null id as a request, unknown-method, notification, shutdown). Two new
  integration tests drive the real binary: `mcp --print-config` and an
  `initialize` round-trip over real stdio.
- An independent review pass drove hardening before merge: a bad-UTF-8 stdin
  line no longer kills the server (byte-oriented read), a single reused runtime
  replaces per-call runtime construction, and a corrupt credentials store
  degrades to an unauthenticated start instead of failing to boot. Each was
  reproduced against the release binary and locked with a test.
- `cargo build --release`, then drove the release binary end-to-end over stdio:
  `initialize` (serverInfo + echoed protocolVersion), `tools/list` (9 tools),
  `tools/call tenants_list` with a base URL but no credential (structured
  `unauthenticated` result naming `stagecraft login`), `stamp_new` without
  posture (-32602), `ping`, clean shutdown on EOF. Verified strict framing (one
  message per physical line, no embedded newlines) and that the text content
  mirrors the structured envelope.
- Spine gates green: `spec-spine compile`, `index` (`stagecraft_cli::mcp`
  resolves, 0 diagnostics), `lint --fail-on-warn` (0/0/0), `index check` fresh.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: this PR implements spec 005 (the MCP face) but necessarily
edits files under the spec 002 crate scaffold: src/mcp.rs (new), src/cli.rs,
src/commands.rs, src/error.rs, src/main.rs, src/verbs/mod.rs, src/verbs/
tenants.rs, src/verbs/stamp.rs, src/verbs/fleet.rs. The crate's
[package.metadata.spec-spine] key couples the whole crate to spec 002, so every
feature spec's code lands in 002 territory; the new logic lives in the
spec-005-owned stagecraft_cli::mcp module, while the verb-layer edits factor the
shared spec-004 request path both faces call, and the src/error.rs edit only
annotates the now-unconstructed not-implemented taxonomy arm (all verbs are
implemented). Waiving rather than editing the completed 002 spec, per the
precedent set by the spec 003 and 004 PRs. Approved by the repo owner as the
standing pattern.

title: feat(004): governance verbs (tenants, stamps, fleet) over the API client
body:
## Summary

Spec 004: the CLI face becomes useful. The stub tenants/stamp/fleet
commands from spec 002 become real calls to the Stagecraft control
plane over the spec 003 API client, each with a stable JSON envelope
the MCP face (spec 005) will reuse.

## What landed

- **New `stagecraft_cli::verbs` module** (spec 004's `establishes`
  symbol): tenants (list/show/install-url, with `--open`), stamp
  (new/status, with `--watch`), fleet (list/deploy/update/backup/
  remove). Human output is aligned tables; `--output json` emits the
  `{ok, data|error}` passthrough envelope, wrapping the plane's payload
  verbatim so the contract stays stable as fields grow.
- **Generalized the API client** (spec 003's `api` module): GET/POST/
  DELETE returning `serde_json::Value`, a body-carrying request path,
  an empty 2xx decoding to JSON null, GET-only retry unchanged. The
  typed `whoami` path routes through the same pipeline.
- **Guards are product surface**: `--posture` is required with no
  default (the platform rejects defaulted postures); `fleet remove`
  carries the confirm name in the DELETE body, with no `--force`/`--yes`
  shortcut.
- **Missing-service 404** surfaces as "not enabled on this control
  plane" (exit 1, not a crash), per spec 004 §1.
- JSON-mode failures render `{ok:false,error}` on stdout via a new
  `AppError::Rendered` (exit 1, no doubled stderr line). A stamp or
  fleet record with no readable `id`/`status` is a decode error, not a
  blank (§5.3), so `--watch` cannot spin on a statusless response.

## Design decisions (spec 004 §5, 2026-07-15 amendment)

Endpoint shapes are grounded in stagecraft specs 004/005/006 and
inlined into §5.1 as the CLI's expectation. One endpoint is
CLI-inlined: `fleet list` maps to GET `/tenants/:id/fleet`, because
platform spec 006 defines deploy/status/update/backup/remove but no
list; the CLI adds the symmetric collection GET (mirroring
`GET /tenants/:id/stamps`). §1 governs if a live plane diverges.

## Testing

72 tests (60 unit + 12 integration): per-verb happy path, api-error
surfacing, missing-service 404 mapping, watch-mode terminal states, the
statusless-response guard, and a JSON envelope snapshot per verb family.
The release binary was driven end-to-end against a mock plane: every
verb renders correctly in both formats, exit codes are right, the
non-idempotent DELETE is not retried, and `--debug` never leaks the
token.

## Status: stays `implementation: in-progress`

The §3 manual e2e against a live plane cannot run: stagecraft's
tenants/factory/fleet services (its specs 004/005/006) are all
`implementation: pending`, so no reachable plane serves these
endpoints. All mock-testable acceptance holds; the live check unblocks
when a plane exists. Dated Status note added to the spec (§6).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: this PR implements the spec 004 verb surface but
necessarily edits files under the spec 002 crate scaffold and the spec
003 api module (src/api.rs, src/cli.rs, src/commands.rs, src/error.rs,
src/main.rs, tests/cli.rs). The crate's [package.metadata.spec-spine]
key couples the whole crate to spec 002, and spec 003 owns the API
client this builds on; the new logic lives in the spec-004-owned
stagecraft_cli::verbs module, while the edits to 002/003 territory are
the wiring: command arguments, dispatch, the client's new GET/POST/
DELETE verbs, and the JSON error-envelope exit path. Waiving rather
than editing the completed 002/003 specs, per the precedent set by
spec 003's PR. Approved by the repo owner.

title: feat(003): auth + control-plane API client (login, whoami, api module)
body:
## Summary

Implements spec 003 (auth + control-plane API client): the `auth` and `api` modules, `stagecraft login` (browser-assisted bearer-token handoff) and `stagecraft whoami`, a 0600 per-base-url credentials store, a uniform API error taxonomy, GET-only retry with jitter, and a global `--debug` flag.

The auth mechanism is recorded in the spec: the preferred RFC 8252 loopback OIDC flow needs control-plane additions that do not exist yet (a public rauthy client with a loopback redirect, and a token-return endpoint), so the paste fallback is the sanctioned v1. The credentials store and bearer replay are independent of acquisition, so the loopback flow drops in later with no change to the store or the api module.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` (36 tests: credentials 0600 round-trip and stale-temp tightening, GET-only retry, 401 to login hint, whoami happy/sad via httpmock, whoami JSON shape)
- `spec-spine compile && spec-spine index check && spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn && spec-spine couple`

Manual e2e against a live control plane is deferred per spec section 1: the control plane is pre-code, so no plane is reachable. Spec 003 stays implementation: in-progress with a dated Status note until that check can run.

Spec-Drift-Waiver: spec 003 fills in the scaffold that spec 002 established. 002 section 2 placed the src/ tree and the login/whoami command stubs specifically "so later specs fill them in" and predicted "Async arrives with spec 003 (tokio + reqwest)". The 002-owned paths changed here (Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, src/cli.rs, src/commands.rs) together with the new src/api.rs and src/auth.rs modules that 003 establishes are exactly that scaffold fill-in; no 002 design is contradicted, so this is a coupling waiver, not a coherence override.

title: feat(002): stagecraft crate scaffold, layered config, CI
body:
## Spec 002: crate scaffold, config, CI

Implements `specs/002-crate-scaffold/spec.md`: the single `stagecraft`
binary that every later verb hangs off. No network I/O yet (auth and the
API client arrive in 003).

### What lands
- **Command tree** (clap derive): stub verbs (`login`/`whoami`,
  `tenants`, `stamp`, `fleet`, `mcp`) whose `--help` names the owning
  spec and whose handlers exit 2; working `version`, `config show`, and
  `completions <shell>`.
- **Layered config**: `flags > env (STAGECRAFT_*) > config file >
  default`, resolved by a pure, unit-tested function. `config show`
  prints the effective value of each field with its source.
- **Output discipline**: one layer, human text on a TTY and stable JSON
  with `--output json`. JSON shapes are treated as API from the first
  verb (the MCP face in 005 reuses them).
- **Exit-code contract**: `0` ok, `1` operational, `2` usage /
  not-implemented; errors go to stderr only.
- **CI** (`ci.yml`): fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, test, release build on a
  SHA-pinned `actions/checkout`. The spec-spine governance gate stays in
  its own `spec-spine.yml` workflow.

### Verification (local)
- `cargo build --release` yields `target/release/stagecraft`; `--help`
  shows the full tree; stubs exit 2 naming their spec; `config show` and
  `completions zsh` work.
- `cargo test`: 18 tests (config precedence per field/source, exit
  codes, JSON shape, stdout hygiene).
- Spine gates green: `compile`, `index`, `lint --fail-on-warn`,
  `index check`, and `couple` (11 paths, no drift).

### Spec change
Amended 002 (before coding, per the backlog protocol) to declare
`clap_complete` in the dependency list: the spec required a working
`completions` verb but omitted the crate that generates the scripts.
Flipped `implementation` to `complete`.

### Note
`directories` resolves the config path per platform (Linux
`~/.config/stagecraft/config.toml`, macOS
`~/Library/Application Support/stagecraft/config.toml`), consistent with
the spec's "via the directories crate" instruction.
